title: Promise
content:
The afternoon sun stood high above the moving train, its warm rays streaming through the windows and filling the coach with a gentle glow. Seated beside each other, Siddu and Sneha quietly enjoyed their lunch as the train continued its journey toward Delhi.

Every now and then, Sneha found herself stealing glances at him.

She observed everything—the way he ate, the calmness in his manners, the warmth in his smile, and even the way he spoke. Without realizing it, her eyes had become accustomed to searching for him every passing moment.

It was the first time she had ever fallen for someone.

The feeling was new, unfamiliar, yet strangely comforting. The more she looked at him, the more she found herself getting lost in his presence, caring for him in ways she couldn't yet explain.

Siddu eventually noticed her lingering gaze.

He looked up with a puzzled smile.

"What happened, Sneha?" he asked. "Why are you looking at me like that? Is there something you want to say?"

Caught off guard, Sneha immediately shook her head.

"No... nothing," she replied, trying to hide her embarrassment.

Then, pointing at his lunchbox, she added with a playful smile,

"Just finish your lunch quickly... and continue your story."

Siddu couldn't help but chuckle.

He simply smiled, nodded in agreement, and quietly resumed eating, while Sneha waited impatiently for the story she was eager to hear.

After finishing their lunch, both of them returned to their seats. The train had picked up speed again, its rhythmic movement filling the brief silence between them.

Sneha settled into her seat before suddenly turning toward Siddu.

"Wait..." she said, raising a finger. "Before you continue, I want to ask you something."

Siddu looked at her curiously.

"What is it?"

She hesitated for a moment before asking softly,

"Are... you still in a relationship?"

For a few seconds, Siddu didn't answer.

Instead, he simply smiled and looked out of the window.

Sneha waited patiently, hoping for a reply.

Finally, he turned back to her.

"You'll know soon," he said gently.

With those words, he continued his story.

________________________________________

"After Shreya and I confessed our feelings to each other, I couldn't wait to share the news with Kiran and Rohini."

"The moment I told Rohini, she became happier than I was."

"I knew it!" she laughed. "I told you both were made for each other!"

Her excitement made me laugh as well.

But when I looked at Kiran...

The smile on my face slowly disappeared.

He looked stunned.

"Are you serious, Sidhu?" he asked. "Did... did Shreya really confess to you?"

I nodded.

"Yes."

For a moment, he didn't say anything. His face was filled with confusion, as though he was trying to understand something that didn't make sense.

"What happened?" I asked. "Why are you reacting like this?"

He forced a faint smile and slowly shook his head.

"It's nothing."

Then he looked at me and said quietly,

"If you're truly confident about your feelings... then follow your heart."

Although he smiled while saying those words, something about his expression felt different.

I couldn't understand what was troubling him.

But instead of thinking too much about it, I pushed those thoughts aside and chose to enjoy the happiness that had finally found its way into my life.

Siddu smiled as countless memories flashed before his eyes.

"From that day onward, every moment I spent with Shreya became a memory I wanted to hold on to forever."

"Every day, we discovered something new about each other."

She would ask about my family, my childhood, my dreams, and the little things that had shaped my life. In return, I would ask about hers. We spoke about our favorite movies, songs, food, colours, places we wanted to visit, and the dreams we hoped to fulfill one day.

There were no secrets between us.

The more we talked, the closer we became.

"Our free periods became our favourite part of the day."

We would often sit by the classroom window together, watching the golden sunset slowly disappear beyond the horizon. Sometimes we talked without stopping, and sometimes we simply sat there in comfortable silence, enjoying each other's company. Strangely, even those silent moments felt more meaningful than words.

After college, neither of us was ever in a hurry to go home.

We would walk side by side through the quiet streets, letting the cool evening breeze accompany us on our way. The conversations never seemed to end. We spoke about everything and nothing at the same time, laughing over the smallest things as if the world belonged only to us.

Siddu paused, a gentle smile lingering on his lips.

"Those days..." he said softly, his eyes fixed on the passing scenery outside the train, "...are still as clear as if they happened yesterday."

"They weren't just memories."

"They became a part of me."

"No matter how many years pass, I don't think I'll ever forget the feeling of walking beside her. Even today, when I close my eyes, those evenings unfold before me as vividly as they did back then."

For a brief moment, silence filled the space between them.

Sneha didn't interrupt.

She simply watched Siddu, realizing that every word he spoke came not from his lips alone, but from a heart that had truly lived those memories.

Siddu's smile grew a little wider as another cherished memory surfaced.

"My birthday came a few weeks later," he said softly. "Shreya insisted that we celebrate it together."

Early that morning, the two of us went shopping.

She spent more time choosing clothes for me than I did. Every shirt she picked up, she would hold it against me and ask with complete seriousness, "Does this look good on you?"

Watching the excitement on her face made me happier than receiving any birthday gift ever could.

After we finished shopping, we had lunch together at a nearby restaurant. From there, we wandered through the mall without any destination in mind.

She laughed freely that day.

She teased me, cracked silly jokes, pulled me into random shops just for fun, and behaved like an excited little child. Seeing her so carefree made me realize that happiness isn't found in places—it is found in the person you're with.

As evening approached, we made our way to the beach.

The setting sun painted the sky in shades of gold and orange. Children chased each other along the shore, families enjoyed the cool breeze, and groups of friends laughed as the waves kissed the sand.

Amid all that life, it felt as though only the two of us existed.

We walked side by side along the shoreline until our legs grew tired.

Finally, we sat down on a quiet bench overlooking the sea.

For a while, neither of us spoke.

The sound of the waves was enough.

Then, without saying a word, Shreya gently slipped her hand into mine.

A strange warmth spread through my heart.

It was such a small gesture...

Yet it made me feel like the happiest person in the world.

Time passed without either of us realizing it. Before long, the sun disappeared beyond the horizon, and the soft glow of the moon quietly took its place, bathing the beach in a gentle silver light.

Shreya broke the silence.

"This..." she said with a smile, "...is the most beautiful day of my life."

"I don't think I'll ever forget it."

A few moments later, her smile slowly faded.

She looked at me with an expression I had never seen before.

"Sidhu..."

"Hmm?"

"Can you promise me something?"

I smiled.

"Anything."

She held my hand a little tighter.

"Promise me..."

"...that you'll never leave me."

"...and that you'll stay with me forever."

For a moment, I simply looked into her eyes.

Then I gently intertwined my fingers with hers and smiled.

"I promise."

I gently squeezed her hand.

"No matter what happens... I'll always be with you."

At that moment, I truly believed it was a promise I would keep for the rest of my life.

I had no idea that fate had already begun writing a different ending.
